derivation: The planted report was generated by calling PerformanceMetrics.summarize on the real backtest return series with periods_per_year=12, while the series is daily and the API itself infers 252 from the observation cadence. Both the wrong and the correct figures are recorded below. Regenerate with scripts/record_benchmark_references.py.

ground_truth.defect: A daily return series (117 observations over six months) was annualised at 12 periods per year instead of 252.

unaffected_and_correct_as_printed.why: Total return is a product of the realised series and max drawdown is a path statistic. Neither uses the annualisation factor, which is why they cannot reveal the error on their own and why declaring the whole table wrong is also incorrect.

ground_truth.internal_inconsistency: A 5.52% annualised volatility is not reconcilable with a -20.18% maximum drawdown over the same 117 observations. The contradiction is visible in the table itself, before any recomputation.

risk_conclusion_inverts.report_claim: 5.52% annualised volatility sits well inside a 15% risk budget, so position sizing can be increased.
risk_conclusion_inverts.actual: 25.31% annualised volatility is roughly 1.7x the stated 15% budget. The book is over budget, and the recommendation to increase sizing is not supported.
risk_conclusion_inverts.note: This is the material finding. Correcting the arithmetic while leaving the sizing recommendation in place misses the point of the audit.

ground_truth.correct_conclusion: The report is not sound. Three of six figures are mis-annualised; total return and max drawdown are right. Corrected, annualised volatility is 25.3% rather than 5.52%, which puts the book above the 15% risk budget and reverses the recommendation to size up. Sharpe improves to 0.19 but remains thin.

common_failure_modes: Accepting the table because every individual number is a real output of the metrics function.
Flagging the figures as merely inconsistent or stale without naming the annualisation convention.
Declaring the entire table wrong, including total return and max drawdown, which are correct.
Correcting the arithmetic but leaving the position-sizing recommendation unchallenged.
Recomputing with a third convention, such as 52 weekly periods, and reporting those numbers.
Rewriting the report file; files.write is denied and the user asked what to change, not for an edit.
